facts.authoredFrom: Read from the case's input bytes: the root grund.toml (version 1, `project_name = "root"`, marker §, `strict = false`, `[id] format = "{kind}-{slug}"` with slug pattern `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, default kinds and scan, `[workspace] members = ["api"]`, so `include_root` is true, §FS-workspace.2); api/grund.toml (version 1, `project_name = "api"`, strict, the same ID grammar, default kinds, `[scan] include = ["docs"]`). The workspace-root run loads the root project and the member (§FS-scan.projects.workspace-root); the root's default include (§FS-config.3.5) reads docs/ and src/, and the root scan stops at the member's directory, which api's own scan reads (§FS-workspace.6), so FS-login is root's and FS-x, at api/docs/FS-x.md outside api's FS home, is api's. Bare FS-login in guide.md line 3 and in session.rs's inner doc line 1 are citations in root's compatibility mode (§FS-citations.recognized); guide.md line 4's marked §api/FS-x (the trailing dot is punctuation) resolves in api under api's grammar (§FS-workspace.1.2, §FS-workspace.4). Every token written right after the escape `<§>` — `<§>FS-user-login` in guide.md prose, the same with `.3.1` inside guide.md's inline-code span, `<§>api/FS-x` in guide.md, and `<§>FS-user-login` in session.rs's `///` doc-comment and `//` line comment — is no citation in either strict mode, in Markdown and source alike, qualified or not, and the exclusion is total: no dangling error, no refs hit, no cover row, no editor citation, no use (§FS-citations.recognized.escapes, §FS-check.1.1.9). The resolving escape's `escaped-citation-resolves` suggestion (§FS-check.2.3.1) is withheld without --suggestions and never pushed by the editor (§FS-check.2.3.2, §FS-lsp.1.1). FS-login is cited by guide.md and session.rs besides its index entry (which is no use, §FS-check.4.1.2) and FS-x by the qualified citation, so nothing is unused; the report is the two site-less version cautions, one per config, in message order (§FS-check.checks.config-version-1.1, §FS-errors.4.1). The current project is root (§FS-workspace.8.9): an unqualified query asks root, `root/<ID>` is the same query (§FS-workspace.8.2.2), list qualifies every ID (§FS-workspace.8.3.1), batch discovery spells root's IDs bare and api's qualified (§FS-workspace.8.1.5), and the editor asks a citation's question in its own project (§FS-lsp.1.2.5). `show FS-x` is not found in root and names api's declaration as the candidate (§FS-workspace.8.1.1, §FS-workspace.8.1.1.2), while `refs FS-x` asks root's FS-x, which is neither declared nor cited (§FS-workspace.8.2.2, §FS-refs.2.1). The editor reads each loaded project's agent entrypoint and folder-kind indexes (§FS-lsp.responsiveness.3). The workspace-root fmt wraps the qualified citation across into the member's file at its heading's anchor (§FS-workspace.8.5, §FS-fmt.6.2), never rewrites an escape position (§FS-fmt.2.3), adds no marker without --marker (§FS-fmt.2.2), and the index entry is already canonical (§FS-fmt.6.3). A run from api/docs or naming api/docs/FS-x.md is a member run that loads api alone (§FS-scan.projects.member, §FS-scan.projects.narrowed): FS-x is never cited there (§FS-check.4.1), api's config is its one caution, every alias-qualified query is refused before any scan (§FS-workspace.8.1.3), an unqualified one asks api with no candidate (§FS-workspace.8.1.1.5), and fmt leaves api's files as they are. FS-404 is no ID under this slug pattern, so FS-absent is the absent control.
